answer: Agents can require each new identity to complete a useful task and post a refundable stake that is slashed if peers verify the work was copied or invalid. A reputation ledger then gives weight to identities with a history of accepted contributions, not to raw account count. An attacker can still create many accounts, but must fund each stake and produce distinct, verifiable work, making a sybil swarm costly to sustain. A sonnet, lotus, or lantern might be a harmless task example; none grants trust by itself.
